# Agents run in CLI harnesses through a bridge

Each session of an agent is its own Claude Code CLI in a herdr pane on the user's machine. The server calls one **harness** contract, and the Claude Code CLI implementation drives its pane through a **bridge** contract, so cmux can take herdr's place and the Claude Agent SDK can take the CLI's without the server changing; each contract's `check` lets onboarding see which bridges and harnesses are installed and save the choice in the database. Claude Code's hooks, passed at launch through `--settings`, post to the local server and are the main status signal; herdr's status and the screen are the fallback, since an Escape fires no hook. Agents message each other as Claude Code peers through its cross-session messaging, which an SDK session on the same machine can join later ([research](../research/0002-harness-bridge.md)).

The words follow the sources where they speak, counted with `bun run terms` on 2026-10-20. `harness(es)?` appears in 9/9, and five define it as this layer, Claude Code, Cloudflare Agents, Mastra, Vercel AI SDK and Vercel eve ("A harness is a complete agent runtime, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Pi", [AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-harnesses/overview); "Claude Code is the harness; Claude is the model inside it", [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary)); `runtimes?` (9/9) appears more often, but names different layers in different places: Cloudflare uses it for the durable layer underneath the harness, and the multi-agent apps that drive CLIs use it for the loop, the adapter around it and the bridge alike. `runners?` (9/9) and `engines?` (7/9) appear as well, but only the OpenAI Agents SDK names this layer a runner (its `Runner`), and none of the multi-agent apps read uses either word for it. Bridge is the user's word for the herdr layer, which no source names, though `bridges?` appears in 8/9 (all but the Claude Agent SDK, whose package still exports `bridge`): Claude Code's Remote Control and that export use it for connecting a running session to a UI elsewhere, while `hosts?`, `terminals?` and `workspaces?` (9/9 each) already carry other meanings, and `multiplexers?` appears in 1/9.

## Considered Options

- **The Claude Agent SDK first:** as the AI SDK's `@ai-sdk/harness-claude-code` does, typed events and answers, but no terminal for a human to watch, and the user starts from the CLIs.
- **The Agent Client Protocol:** structured events from the same CLIs, but its Claude Code and Codex adapters are third-party and there is no terminal to watch either.
- **The screen alone:** no multi-agent app that drives a Claude Code TUI detects a usage limit from the screen, while hooks miss only an Escape.
